output.summary: An erect annual crop whose wild ancestor and origin are unknown, the fava bean has square stems and grey-green leaves without climbing tendrils. Its white flowers have true-black wing spots. The beans are widely eaten, but people with favism must avoid them; boiling for ten minutes destroys most of their relatively low toxin levels.
output.edibilityNote: Beans are eaten raw or cooked; young pods and leaves are also edible. People with favism must avoid them, while boiling reduces most lectin toxins.
